card.title: How To Fix an iPhone 8 That Has No Power. Does Not Boot

source.title: How To Fix an iPhone 8 That Has No Power. Does Not Boot

claims.statement: iPhone 8 / 8 Plus drawing about 2 A before power-on: most likely shorted cap on PP_VDD_MAIN, then PP_VDD_BOOST, display backlight anodes, or PP_SPKRAMP_TOP_VBOOST; inject 4 V / 2 A to find it and remove it.

Liquid-damage hot spots for VDD_MAIN shorts: near BBPMU (C303_E), back top arm (C4190, C4191, C4195, C4196), near WLAN (C7608_W, C7609_W), above the CPU (C3790). A loose screw can short test point TP0526 by the SIM slot to ground.
Tigris MOSFET Q3350 heats instantly when injecting through the battery connector but cannot itself be shorted.
No draw before power-on, then bouncing current after: check PP3V0_NAND, PP0V9_NAND and PP1V8_IO for a shorted cap; PMIC U2700 heats but is not the cause.
Same bouncing pattern with PP1V8_S2 or PP1V1_S2 shorted and heat above the CPU means a RAM short (advanced RAM replacement).

procedure: Inspect for liquid damage and loose screws near TP0526.
Before-boot short: test VDD_MAIN, VDD_BOOST, BL anodes, SPKRAMP VBOOST; inject 4 V / 2 A and remove the hot cap.
After-boot bounce: test NAND rails and PP1V8_IO; then PP1V8_S2 / PP1V1_S2 for RAM short.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
